# `smelt.auth`

<!-- Auto-generated by `cargo xtask gen-lua-docs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Availability:** Everywhere, including headless mode.

Authenticated provider helpers. Requests use smelt-managed credentials without exposing bearer tokens to Lua.

## `smelt.auth.managed_usage`

```lua
fun(provider: string): { summary: table?, limits: table[], plan: string?, credits: string?, resetCredits: table? }?, string?
```

Fetch parsed managed-provider usage. Credentials stay in Rust; Lua receives
provider-neutral rows with `{ label, used, limit, resetAt? }`.
`resetAt` is Unix seconds, formatted by the consumer.
Supported for `codex`, `kimi-code`, and `claude-code` (asks the installed
Claude Code without a model request). Codex also reports plan and credits.
Codex and Claude Code report resetCredits `{ count, inventory?, options? }`:
`inventory` holds `{ expires_at? }` entries, and Claude Code lists the reset
kinds to choose from as `options` of `{ id, label, description, count, expires_at? }`.

## `smelt.auth.redeem_usage_reset`

```lua
fun(provider: string, scope: string, request_id: string, credit_id: string?): string?, string?
```

Redeem one usage limit reset credit of `provider` (`codex` or `claude-code`)
using credentials matching `usage_scope(provider)`. `credit_id` names the
reset option to spend when the report lists `resetCredits.options`.
Reuse `request_id` when retrying an uncertain outcome to avoid a second redemption.

## `smelt.auth.request`

```lua
fun(provider: string, opts: { path: string, method: string?, body: string? }): { status: integer, body: string }?, string?
```

Run an authenticated request against a provider-owned endpoint using
smelt-managed credentials. Credentials stay in Rust; Lua receives only
the HTTP status and body. `opts.path` must be an absolute path without a
URL scheme; `opts.method` defaults to `GET`.

## `smelt.auth.usage_scope`

```lua
fun(provider: string): string?
```

Return an opaque login scope for account-usage caches, or nil when managed credentials are unavailable (including externally authenticated providers). Never contains credentials.
